elements.element: Preferred: no non-solicitation obligation binds Customer at all
elements.evidence: "neither party shall, or shall permit its affiliates to, directly solicit for employment any employee of the other party" — a non-solicit still binds Customer
"neither party shall, or shall permit its affiliates to, directly solicit"

elements.element: Fallback: limited to personnel directly involved in the services
elements.evidence: "any employee of the other party who was directly involved in the provision of services under this Agreement"

elements.element: Fallback: duration is 12 months running from the end of the individual's involvement
elements.evidence: "for a period of twelve (12) months following the end of an individual's involvement in the provision of services under this Agreement"
"does not apply to general advertisements or other recruitment efforts not specifically targeted at the other party's personnel"
"or to any unsolicited approach by an individual"
"solicit for employment" replaces "not to hire"; "This Section does not restrict either party from hiring any person"

offending_extra_words: This Section does not restrict either party from hiring any person
or other recruitment efforts not specifically targeted at the other party's personnel
reasons: All atomic fallback elements are present: mutuality, scope limited to personnel directly involved, 12 months from the end of that involvement (expressly stated), general-advertisement and unsolicited-approach carve-outs, and no no-hire; the drafter's locked fallback level is satisfied.
Preferred (no non-solicit on Customer) is not met because a mutual non-solicit still binds Customer — acceptable given the locked fallback target.
Minimality fails: the edit is a whole-clause rewrite expanding 62 words to 98 (ratio 1.58) with a 0.77 changed-character ratio, exceeding the official gates.
The added sentence "This Section does not restrict either party from hiring any person" is duplicative — replacing "hire" with "solicit for employment" already removes the no-hire covenant.
"or other recruitment efforts not specifically targeted at the other party's personnel" is a broader carve-out than the playbook's general-advertisement carve-out and is surplus wording.
No unrelated commercial term is disturbed and no undefined term or dangling mechanic is introduced, so intent is preserved.
